<span id="paper-foundation-models-xla-trenches-c37e2d34" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-80a43e3611b0011e">Why don&#x27;t successful compilation and crash-free execution establish XLA correctness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Axla-trenches">XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Silent miscompilations can return finite, correctly shaped tensors while indexing, rounding, buffers, or synchronization are wrong. Completion and briefly normal loss miss failures with no error signal. The paper uses differential references on valid inputs plus hierarchical isolation, not launch success as correctness evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: A narrow-integer iota wrap can make a write at index 5 also modify 261. Execution completes; comparison against correct indexing semantics exposes it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制与数值例子. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2611.00624-xla-trenches/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80a43e3611b0011e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:xla-trenches" data-paper-title="XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-098b3c2d60311839">Why combine backward input constraints with VREG inspection inside intact fusions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Axla-trenches">XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Backward constraints prevent invalid inputs such as negative square roots or division by zero from creating false differences. Macro isolation only finds a fusion; lowering faults inside it still require register intermediates. Splitting it changes memory precision and pipelining and can hide the bug, so a correct split graph does not validate the original fusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: r=x−f32(f16(x)) becomes zero if VREG rounding is skipped. Splitting for debugging can spill to 16-bit HBM and restore rounding. Inspect the original fusion rather than replacing it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心机制与数值例子, 资源与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2611.00624-xla-trenches/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-098b3c2d60311839">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:xla-trenches" data-paper-title="XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0719ea969a0fdbee">Why are 142 resolved bugs, 103 under review, and online A/B gains three different kinds of evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Axla-trenches">XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Resolved counts describe defects closed through engineering review. Pending findings can still be rejected or revised, so they do not make 245 resolved bugs. User A/B requires actual randomized comparisons and business metrics, not inference from bug counts. The paper qualifies as Google systems infrastructure, not as industrial recommendation evidence passing an A/B gate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Of 10 submitted patches, if 6 landed and 4 are pending, 6 are completed, not 10. Even landing all 10 supplies no randomized CTR experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 论文工程与线上证据, 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2611.00624-xla-trenches/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0719ea969a0fdbee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:xla-trenches" data-paper-title="XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c830109380a835e9">With OpenXLA public, why mark the full paper not reproduced instead of running an A100 substitute?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Axla-trenches">XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Public macro isolation and evaluation are only part of the pipeline. Production graphs, the internal agent harness, target ISA/MXU simulation, VREG hardware stepping, and physical-TPU confirmation do not come with the framework. A100 has different register, rounding, and compilation semantics; a CUDA example cannot validate TPU defects. Resource and availability mismatch justifies review DONE/not reproduced rather than fabricated success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Correctly executing two casts in CUDA does not show that TPU lowering retained them. Matching outputs do not cover the original TPU-generated code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 已核查与未实现, 资源与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2611.00624-xla-trenches/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c830109380a835e9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:activation-model-scanner" data-paper-title="Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-activation-model-scanner-171bac1e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c950ffb6691c1f4">Why scan contrastive input activations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aactivation-model-scanner">Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Identify safety-related separation in intermediate layers and compare direction/drift with a matched baseline. This does not generate or validate behavioral answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Separable concepts do not guarantee all related requests are handled well.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05578">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2608.05578-activation-model-scanner/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c950ffb6691c1f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:activation-model-scanner" data-paper-title="Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2aacee6d37ba8428">Why doesn&#x27;t AMS activation separation establish behavioral safety?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aactivation-model-scanner">Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mid-layer contrast directions and same-architecture baseline drift provide structural evidence only. Layer numbering, variance, and baseline affect thresholds. Independent behavior evaluation is still required.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model can distinguish safety concepts internally while still responding unsafely to a particular prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05578">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2608.05578-activation-model-scanner/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2aacee6d37ba8428">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:activation-model-scanner" data-paper-title="Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">

<h2 id="qa-bc23a004bfa13d4a">What do AMS Tier 1 and Tier 2 measure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aactivation-model-scanner">Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tier 1 measures separation of positive and negative projections. Tier 2 compares direction consistency and relative drift against matching layers/dimensions. Internal separation need not mean baseline alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Wide separation can coexist with a direction flip relative to baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05578">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2608.05578-activation-model-scanner/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc23a004bfa13d4a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:activation-model-scanner" data-paper-title="Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-00d402cba51d2174">Why add one to the AMS block index in Hugging Face hidden_states?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aactivation-model-scanner">Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Block hooks are zero-based but hidden_states[0] is embeddings. Use block_id+1, select the last real token, and preserve population variance and strict threshold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Block 9 reads hidden_states[10].</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05578">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2608.05578-activation-model-scanner/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-00d402cba51d2174">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:combinatorial-watermark" data-paper-title="Detecting Post-generation Edits to Watermarked LLM Outputs via Combinatorial Watermarking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-combinatorial-watermark-183aedb0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c09d9ae85d58f347">Why bias vocabulary partitions by a periodic pattern?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Acombinatorial-watermark">Detecting Post-generation Edits to Watermarked LLM Outputs via Combinatorial Watermarking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Minnesota</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tag-specific logit biases induce a statistical periodic structure. The detector compares windows across all cyclic shifts for watermark and edit evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>AB partition alternation is detectable without knowing where the observed text starts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.01637v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2510.01637-combinatorial-watermark/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c09d9ae85d58f347">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:combinatorial-watermark" data-paper-title="Detecting Post-generation Edits to Watermarked LLM Outputs via Combinatorial Watermarking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-66b97bbf9772dff1">Why can testing all cyclic phases still miss full-period deletion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Acombinatorial-watermark">Detecting Post-generation Edits to Watermarked LLM Outputs via Combinatorial Watermarking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Minnesota</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Phase search handles global offsets, but deleting a whole period can preserve the repeating pattern and phase. Independently calibrate global/local thresholds; a hard-pattern diagnostic is not perfect soft-watermark localization. No full local model edit matrix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing one full red/blue cycle leaves the remaining pattern unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.01637v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2510.01637-combinatorial-watermark/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66b97bbf9772dff1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:combinatorial-watermark" data-paper-title="Detecting Post-generation Edits to Watermarked LLM Outputs via Combinatorial Watermarking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9acb87bf75defb5d">Can global D and local E(t) thresholds replace each other?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Acombinatorial-watermark">Detecting Post-generation Edits to Watermarked LLM Outputs via Combinatorial Watermarking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Minnesota</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>D detects a watermark across the whole passage; E(t) uses window coverage to flag possible edits. They differ in scope and threshold direction. Calibrate false positives independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Global passage can pass while a short span scores low; that does not precisely identify every edit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.01637v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2510.01637-combinatorial-watermark/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9acb87bf75defb5d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:combinatorial-watermark" data-paper-title="Detecting Post-generation Edits to Watermarked LLM Outputs via Combinatorial Watermarking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb75a73b696eddd8">Can local E(t) zero-pad edges?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Acombinatorial-watermark">Detecting Post-generation Edits to Watermarked LLM Outputs via Combinatorial Watermarking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Minnesota</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is defined only for complete interior t=w−1 through T−w, without zero padding or changing denominators. Check all phases and preserve full-period deletion as a blind negative control.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Edge positions with incomplete windows should not be falsely flagged because zeros were added.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.01637v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2510.01637-combinatorial-watermark/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb75a73b696eddd8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:criticl" data-paper-title="CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-criticl-4a912854" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-429d311a384d5142">Why build CritBank from weak-model errors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Acriticl">CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cluster recurring failures offline into reusable reminders for stronger models. This moves reflection cost upstream and avoids requiring a first failure on each deployed request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Add a common missed-unit-conversion reminder before a new answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2608.27455-criticl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-429d311a384d5142">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:criticl" data-paper-title="CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a53e3dc987414704">Why doesn&#x27;t CritICL need the strong model to fail first at deployment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Acriticl">CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline weak-model failures become reusable critiques. Static mode uses common patterns and dynamic mode retrieves question-relevant ones before one strong-model generation. Transfer patterns, not weak answers; relevance and coverage matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieve a unit-conversion reminder before answering, without reading test gold to craft it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2608.27455-criticl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a53e3dc987414704">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:criticl" data-paper-title="CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-72ab8c1467b98e00">How do static and dynamic critique selection differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Acriticl">CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Static uses frequent global failures; dynamic retrieves relevant CritBank entries for the current input. Both act before generation, but only dynamic adds input-dependent retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A math question can retrieve calculation reminders different from those for other requests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2608.27455-criticl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72ab8c1467b98e00">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:criticl" data-paper-title="CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-496c385698250dff">Why not select critiques with the current question&#x27;s correct answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Acriticl">CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>That leaks evaluation targets into prompts. Dynamic retrieval uses only input similarity to the existing bank and then generates once. Offline failures and current hidden gold stay separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Looking up the solution before picking the critique that fixes it is not deployable retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2608.27455-criticl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-496c385698250dff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:cross-lingual-exploration" data-paper-title="Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-cross-lingual-exploration-96009007" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc3fd0b5d67ab87f">Why explore multiple languages for one knowledge question?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Across-lingual-exploration">Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hebrew University of Jerusalem</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Knowledge may be more accessible under some language contexts. Explore across languages then aggregate semantic answers, not mere string translations or presumed-correct majority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Distinct expressions may refer to one entity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24579v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2606.24579-cross-lingual-exploration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc3fd0b5d67ab87f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:cross-lingual-exploration" data-paper-title="Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-51de139df064f40c">Why not replace cross-lingual semantic aggregation with string voting, and why count aggregation cost?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Across-lingual-exploration">Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hebrew University of Jerusalem</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different languages may phrase equivalent facts differently, and superficially similar errors can differ. The method uses an LM for majority/minority-aware aggregation and separate correctness/consistency judgment. All path and aggregation tokens count. This is literature-only locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two names for one city need entity matching, not separate votes or costs counted from only one path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24579v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2606.24579-cross-lingual-exploration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51de139df064f40c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:cross-lingual-exploration" data-paper-title="Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-730b132540b80efd">Why can&#x27;t a string counter substitute for semantic model aggregation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Across-lingual-exploration">Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hebrew University of Jerusalem</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equivalent meanings can use different strings and equal strings can differ in context. An LM performs majority/minority-aware aggregation and semantic judgments in the paper.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>“United States” and “USA” can be one answer, despite string counts splitting them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24579v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2606.24579-cross-lingual-exploration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-730b132540b80efd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:cross-lingual-exploration" data-paper-title="Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-023dadc002ad7698">Why count more than generated path tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Across-lingual-exploration">Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hebrew University of Jerusalem</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Include each path&#x27;s inputs and aggregation model tokens; semantic correctness and consistency also use model calls. Local work did not run the APIs or provide heuristics as substitutes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten short generations can still produce a long, expensive aggregation prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24579v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2606.24579-cross-lingual-exploration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-023dadc002ad7698">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:deepsea" data-paper-title="DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-deepsea-86ba1d33" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c952637f784a5e5b">Why not report only one DeepSEA multilingual average?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adeepsea">DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Language-resource strata and tasks expose gaps hidden by a mean. The project provides data and evaluation protocol, not a parameter-training algorithm.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>High-resource successes can mask low-resource failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26155v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.26155-deepsea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c952637f784a5e5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:deepsea" data-paper-title="DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8cb698c67be1a136">Why fix prediction order and isolate gold in grouped DeepSEA reporting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adeepsea">DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Validate language, size, and order so predictions align to their examples. Expose only public task fields; keep answers and annotations with the evaluator. This evaluates lower-resource languages, not model training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swapped outputs across languages become alignment errors; the predictor must not see references.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与评分口径. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26155v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.26155-deepsea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8cb698c67be1a136">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:deepsea" data-paper-title="DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-599f68d2d3a3631c">Are deterministic scorers and LLM judges interchangeable in DeepSEA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adeepsea">DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Follow the fixed upstream protocol for each task. Substituting judges changes comparability. Bind outputs to language, subject, and row; group summaries do not fix misalignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Pairing language A row one with a language B answer invalidates scoring even if row counts match.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 公共输入与 Gold 隔离. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26155v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.26155-deepsea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-599f68d2d3a3631c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:deepsea" data-paper-title="DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-67c358643609ee55">Should prediction callbacks get the evaluator or benchmark file and promise not to read gold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adeepsea">DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use allowlisted immutable public input and separate deep-copied private references. Reject missing languages, bad counts, or nonstring outputs. This is data-flow isolation, not an OS sandbox; do not add shell bypasses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Provide question, options, and context, not raw answer_with_cot records.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 公共输入与 Gold 隔离. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26155v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.26155-deepsea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67c358643609ee55">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:detector-scope" data-paper-title="Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-detector-scope-a45f37d9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d312990e6a285659">Why make detection depend on inspectable sparse features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adetector-scope">Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pool SAE features, filter unreliable concept descriptions, and fit a sparse linear head so logits decompose into actual computed contributions rather than post-hoc reasons.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Verify a contribution by zeroing its feature rather than trusting generated explanations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30006v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d312990e6a285659">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:detector-scope" data-paper-title="Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cf2ae2f87e6ebcb4">Why is zeroing a DetectorScope concept exact in logit space but not equivalent to editing text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adetector-scope">Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse pooled features feed a linear head, so each weight times activation is an exact contribution. Text edits can change several features and contexts. Automatic descriptions are imperfect; local head excludes the full SAE/explanation pipeline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Zero one feature to verify its score change; deleting a word can alter several concepts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30006v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cf2ae2f87e6ebcb4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:detector-scope" data-paper-title="Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2d18e295a89d2470">Is description validation equivalent to human confirmation of concept semantics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adetector-scope">Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Spearman correlation compares observed and predicted activation ranks as a filter, not manual validation or safety. Constant sequences do not support the correlation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correlation on a small sample does not prove meanings are correct for every text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30006v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2d18e295a89d2470">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:detector-scope" data-paper-title="Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c1a5afb8140989d8">Why not apply an L1 subgradient and soft thresholding together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adetector-scope">Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Apply BCE SGD with momentum, then ηλ soft thresholding, without a second L1 gradient or bias penalty. Fit uncentered RMS on training only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Penalizing twice changes effective sparsity beyond λ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与结果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
